title: before round 1 check that each path argument in a slice Check command exists in the worktree

sections.heading: Why
sections.body:
`SliceCheckCommandWarnings` (`internal/engine/brief.go:794`) checks only the first word of each Check entry. A Check command whose argument names a path that does not exist gets through to round 1, and round 1 then fails on the spec rather than on the product code. The evidence from S597 is `gofmt -l ./roles`, which failed with `lstat ./roles: no such file or directory`.

Owner decision adj 614 (`checks.path-arguments`, Jon, 2026-11-27): a relative word with a `/` or a leading `./` is a path argument. Flags, URLs, quoted patterns, globs (including `./...`) and absolute paths are not. A missing path argument that is not a Files-created path is a finding. Both callers already turn a finding into a refusal. The plan refuses `run.start` at `internal/daemon/runs.go:1112`. The spec check reports the item as not ready at `internal/daemon/speccheck.go:324`. The spec-draft check (`CheckDraftCheck`, `internal/engine/specdraft.go:158`) uses the same function, so it reports the finding too. Extending the one function covers all three paths.

Owner decisions, 2026-11-27: adj 614 (a missing path argument refuses the start) and adj 615 (a directory that holds a Files path is exempt).

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
Engine, in `internal/engine/brief_test.go`:
- TestSliceCheckCommandWarningsFlagsAMissingPathArgument: existing internal/ok/ and scripts/ok.sh; only ./roles and internal/missing warn with the specified exact message.
- TestSliceCheckCommandWarningsSkipsWordsThatAreNotPaths: exercise every exclusion in the original spec, with a missing-path control so the test fails before wiring exists. Also exclude values after -run, -bench and -skip, rev:path words, and import paths github.com/x/y and charm.land/z (review fix round 1). Each added case must fail before the fix.
- TestSliceCheckCommandWarningsExemptsAFilesPathArgument: exempt scripts/new.sh, ./docs/new.md:3-9 and internal/newpkg/x_test.go, and their parent directories (adj 615); flag an unlisted missing path.
- TestSliceCheckCommandWarningsChecksEachPartOfAChain: go vet ./... && gofmt -l ./roles warns only for ./roles; also cover pipe stages.
- TestSliceCheckCommandWarningsReportsOneWarningForEachMissingPath: ls ./a ./b ./a warns once per distinct word in order.
Engine, in `internal/engine/specdraft_test.go`:
- TestCheckDraftCheckFlagsAMissingPathArgument: CheckDraftCheck (internal/engine/specdraft.go:158) reports the exact Check problem for ./roles; changing Files to roles/x.go exempts its parent per decided adj 615.
Daemon:
- TestRunStartRefusesAMissingCheckPathArgument in `internal/daemon/runs_test.go`: plan warns, start refuses with CodeRefused and item/path/fix text, creates no run; creating roles makes start succeed (internal/daemon/runs.go:1112).
- TestSpecCheckReportsNotReadyForAMissingCheckPathArgument in `internal/daemon/speccheck_test.go`: Ready false with one finding, no questions, role request or cache; creating roles makes it ready (internal/daemon/speccheck.go:324).
- Fix pre-existing fixtures found by go test ./... only where they name missing Check paths.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
1. In `internal/engine/check.go`, add `quoted bool` to `shellWord`. Set it in `scanWord` when the word had a quote or a backslash escape removed. Nothing else about `scanWord` or `simpleCommands` changes.
2. In `internal/engine/brief.go`, add `isPathArgument(w shellWord) bool`. It is true when the word is not quoted, not dynamic (no `*?[]{}$` or backtick, no leading `~`), and does not start with `-`. It must also not be absolute, must contain `/`, must not contain `://`, and must not end in `...`. A leading `./` always satisfies the `/` rule.
3. Add `missingPathArguments(command, files, worktree string) []string`. It walks `simpleCommands(command)`. For each simple command it skips leading `NAME=value` words (`envAssignment`) and the command word, then tests every remaining word with `isPathArgument`. This covers each `&&` part and each pipe stage. Redirect targets are already dropped by `simpleCommands`.
4. For a path argument, strip a leading `./`, join it to the worktree and use `filepath.Rel`. A path that resolves outside the worktree is skipped, because ork already runs those lines through the orchestrator (`plainCheckRow`). `os.Lstat` decides existence, and only `fs.ErrNotExist` counts as missing.
5. A missing path is exempt when it matches a Files path, in backticks with `lineAnchor` and a leading `./` removed and `filepath.Clean` applied. This is the same map that `checkCommandWarnings` already builds from `backticked`, so reuse it. Exempting a missing parent directory of a Files path depends on the owner's answer under Owner needed. With option 1, a missing path is also exempt when a Files path lies under it.
6. In `checkCommandWarnings`, after an entry's first-word check passes, append one warning for each distinct missing path argument, in word order: `Check entry %q: path argument %q does not exist in the worktree`. An entry that already gets the first-word warning keeps the existing `continue` and gets no path warnings. The text is the same for the plan, the spec check and the draft check.
7. `SliceCheckCommandWarnings`, `CheckBodyCommandWarnings`, `runs.go:926` and `speccheck.go:324` need no change. Before the worktree exists, the project checkout stands in for it, as for the first word.
8. Update `docs/design.md` in the paragraph at line 3489. Say that a backticked Check entry also warns for each relative word with `/` that does not exist and is not listed in Files. Say that flags, URLs, quoted words, globs and `./...`, absolute paths and paths outside the worktree are not paths. Say that the refusal and the spec-check finding use the same warnings. Cite adj 614.
9. Add the tests under Failing tests, and see each fail before the change. Fix any existing fixture that fails because it names a missing path, by adding the path to the tree or to Files.
10. Add the changelog entry with `slicer changelog add S615 --text "..."`. Do not edit `CHANGELOG.md`.

sections.heading: Check
sections.body:
Acceptance criteria:
- A backticked Check entry with a relative path argument that does not exist in the worktree (or in the checkout before the worktree exists) and is not listed in Files is a warning. The warning names the entry and the word.
- That warning refuses run.start before a role starts, holds the item in the spec check with Ready false, and shows as a problem on a changed Check section in a spec draft.
- Flags, URLs, quoted words, globs (including ./...), absolute paths, paths outside the worktree and command words are never path arguments.
- An existing path, and a missing path listed in Files, gives no warning.

Commands:
- `go test -run TestSliceCheckCommandWarningsFlagsAMissingPathArgument ./internal/engine` passes.
- `go test -run TestSliceCheckCommandWarningsSkipsWordsThatAreNotPaths ./internal/engine` passes.
- `go test -run TestSliceCheckCommandWarningsExemptsAFilesPathArgument ./internal/engine` passes.
- `go test -run TestSliceCheckCommandWarningsChecksEachPartOfAChain ./internal/engine` passes.
- `go test -run TestSliceCheckCommandWarningsReportsOneWarningForEachMissingPath ./internal/engine` passes.
- `go test -run TestCheckDraftCheckFlagsAMissingPathArgument ./internal/engine` passes.
- `go test -run TestRunStartRefusesAMissingCheckPathArgument ./internal/daemon` passes.
- `go test -run TestSpecCheckReportsNotReadyForAMissingCheckPathArgument ./internal/daemon` passes.
- `go test ./...` passes.
- `go vet ./...` exits 0.
- `gofmt -l .` prints nothing.
- `slicer check` exits 0.
